issues.reason: *Conditional properties* explicitly routes 'a locative or domain PP restricting a kind-level claim' into the condition slot and forbids stripping the restriction, so the parse applied the closest stated rule and asserted nothing at large; the same section registers cond_prop's firing behaviour as an engine-side caveat that 'does not change what you emit'.

The structural observation stands — the no-splitting principle for a multi-atom predicate under a scope operator (*Negation (copular)*) argues for keeping 'immoral thing' whole — but it is stated only for denials, and (Inheritance homosexuality thing) is a bleached typing atom true independently of the attribution, so nothing false or over-asserted reached the KB.

gaps_confirmed: evidential / attribution frame 'According to <source>, P' — nothing records that P is a source's claim rather than a fact; the impersonal-reported-attitude route requires a considered/said/thought/believed matrix verb, and the framing-domain-PP rule covers the field a claim is made in, not its attributed holder
new_gaps: ConditionalProperty has a single property slot, so a multi-atom predicate ('an immoral thing') under a restriction has no licensed way to be kept whole — which is what forces the split the reviewer objects to
the framing / domain-PP oblique needs a symbol for what-is-claimed, and a kind-level property claim has no witness for an (AccordingTo …) oblique to attach to
notes: The parse's decisive virtue is that it never asserts the bare (Inheritance homosexuality immoral), which the condition-slot rule expressly forbids stripping to. The attribution-versus-condition difference is a real expressive loss, but it is a gap rather than a false atom.
